# Data Loss Prevention for ChatGPT Enterprise with Microsoft Purview: Options Compared

## Executive Summary

True, real-time DLP enforcement against ChatGPT Enterprise is **not natively supported by Microsoft Purview** when ChatGPT Enterprise is integrated as a Purview data source. The Purview ChatGPT Enterprise connector is a **post-hoc governance, audit, classification, retention, eDiscovery, and insider-risk surface**, not an inline blocking control. The 24-hour ingestion latency, lack of sensitivity-label and DLP support, and the connector's preview status make it unsuitable as a primary DLP control plane.

To achieve genuine DLP for ChatGPT Enterprise, organizations must layer multiple controls. The recommended approach for a corporate environment is **defense-in-depth**:

1. **Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP + Edge for Business inline protection** (best UX and broad coverage for managed Windows devices, including blocking of prompts/typed input to consumer AI sites in Edge; the same controls can target chatgpt.com and oaiusercontent.com).
2. **Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access (Internet Access) + Microsoft Purview Network Data Security** (broadest cross-browser/cross-app coverage via SASE, with real-time block/audit for unmanaged AI including ChatGPT).
3. **Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps** (CASB) discovery, sanctioning, and session policy for **unsanctioned** AI apps (works for chatgpt.com but session policies require the app to be on Entra-registered app routes, limiting utility for ChatGPT Enterprise).
4. **ChatGPT Enterprise native admin/API controls** (Compliance API, Admin keys, EKM, data residency, ZDR) for governance and export, **not** for inline blocking.

Copilot for Microsoft 365 + Purview DLP is the only Microsoft stack that delivers **truly native, in-product prompt-time DLP**, but it is not "DLP for ChatGPT Enterprise"; it is DLP for Copilot.

---

## 1) Does ChatGPT Enterprise Have Native Purview DLP Support?

**No.** The official Microsoft Purview capability table for ChatGPT Enterprise explicitly marks "Data loss prevention" as **not supported (✕)** ([Microsoft Learn, *Use Microsoft Purview to manage data security & compliance for ChatGPT Enterprise*](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-chatgpt-enterprise)).

Full capability matrix from Microsoft's own documentation:

| Capability | Supported for ChatGPT Enterprise |
|---|---|
| DSPM and DSPM for AI (classic) | ✓ |
| Auditing | ✓ |
| Data classification | ✓ |
| Sensitivity labels | ✕ |
| Encryption without sensitivity labels | ✕ |
| **Data loss prevention** | **✕** |
| Insider Risk Management | ✓ |
| Communication compliance | ✓ |
| eDiscovery | ✓ |
| Data Lifecycle Management | ✓ |
| Compliance Manager | ✓ |

The connector ([learn.microsoft.com/.../archive-chatgpt-interactions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/archive-chatgpt-interactions)) explicitly limits the connector scope:

- **Full scan, incremental scan, classification**: Yes
- **Labeling, access policy, lineage, data sharing, live view**: No
- **Data extracted**: only "text prompts" and "text responses" (no file content, no images)
- **Latency**: "Due to OpenAI's current API limitations, conversations are ingested 24 hours after they occur."
- **Scan trigger**: chatgpt.com data source must be registered in the Microsoft Purview governance portal, with API key stored in Azure Key Vault, and an OpenAI Compliance API key with manually-scoped read/delete permissions (you email support@openai.com to have the scope assigned; the OpenAI portal does not let you self-scope it yet).
- **Billing**: Requires pay-as-you-go billing on top of the Purview account.

Microsoft's own comparison site states bluntly: *"ChatGPT did not enforce Microsoft Purview policies and exposed confidential information"* ([microsoft.com/.../copilot-vs-chatgpt-enterprise](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/copilot-vs-chatgpt-enterprise)). The connector is positioned by Microsoft as a **discovery and governance** capability, not as a control plane for blocking data in flight.

### What the connector is good for
- Pulling historical prompt/response text into DSPM for AI reports and Activity Explorer for after-the-fact review.
- Surfacing risky prompts into Insider Risk Management ("Risky AI usage" template) and Communication Compliance policies.
- Subjecting ingested text to DLP **sensitive information type** classifiers and surfacing matches in Activity Explorer. This is *detection* of what was already shared, not prevention.
- Retention (Data Lifecycle Management) and eDiscovery of past interactions.
- Compliance Manager regulatory templates for AI.

### What the connector cannot do
- Block a prompt at submission time.
- Honor sensitivity labels, encrypt content, or read MIP-protected content.
- Inspect uploaded files.
- Provide sub-24-hour detection (because of the OpenAI Compliance API ingestion delay).
- Replace any real-time DLP control.

**Verdict:** The Purview connector alone is **not a DLP solution for ChatGPT Enterprise**. It is a downstream audit/compliance feed.

### Implementation steps (connector only)
1. Enable pay-as-you-go billing in the Microsoft Purview account.
2. Create an Azure Key Vault and grant Key Vault Administrator and Secret User roles to the Purview data source admin.
3. Request an OpenAI Compliance API key from your ChatGPT Enterprise workspace owner. Email support@openai.com with the last 4 digits of the API key, key name, created-by name, and the requested scope (read, delete, or both). Microsoft Purview needs at least **read** scope.
4. In the Purview governance portal, register ChatGPT Enterprise as a data source. Enter the Workspace ID, domain, and collection.
5. Create a Key Vault credential for the scan.
6. Create a collection policy (either the one-click "DSPM for AI – Capture interactions for enterprise AI apps" or a custom Enterprise AI apps collection policy).
7. Run an initial full scan, then schedule incremental scans.
8. Build DSPM for AI reports filtering on "Enterprise AI apps" / "ChatGPT Enterprise".
9. Create an Insider Risk Management "Risky AI usage" policy and a Communication Compliance policy scoped to the captured data.
10. (Optional) Create a Data Lifecycle Management retention policy with the location "Enterprise AI apps".

### Trade-offs and limitations
- **24-hour ingestion delay** means exfiltration detection is post-hoc.
- Preview-grade; Microsoft explicitly says "These features only apply to the enterprise version of ChatGPT" and consumer ChatGPT must be handled via separate Network Data Security / Edge for Business controls.
- No sensitivity-label awareness, so encrypted/protected content is invisible to the connector.
- No file-content inspection; only text prompts and responses.
- Requires an additional Azure subscription for Key Vault and pay-as-you-go.
- Several message-center items (MC1072396, MC1182689, MC1181998) are still marked as preview or recently rolling out.

---

## 2) Copilot for Microsoft 365 + Purview as an Alternative

This is **not DLP for ChatGPT Enterprise**; it is a different product. But it is the only Microsoft path that delivers **true native, inline DLP for AI prompts at submission time**, which is the closest analogue to "DLP for an AI assistant" inside the Microsoft stack.

Microsoft Purview provides a dedicated DLP policy location called **"Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat"** ([learn.microsoft.com/.../dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about)). Three enforcement actions are supported, and they are independent rule types (per Microsoft, SIT and label conditions **cannot be combined in a single rule**):

1. **Block sensitive prompts** (preview, Nov 2025 → GA targeted late March 2026, per MC1181998). Real-time SIT scan of the prompt text. When matched: Copilot does not respond, and the prompt is not used for external web search or internal Microsoft Graph grounding. Condition: SIT only. Action: "Prevent Copilot from processing content → Processing prompts".
2. **Block external web search on sensitive prompts**. Same SIT condition, but allows Copilot to answer using internal data. Action: "Prevent Copilot from processing content → Performing Web Searches".
3. **Block sensitive labeled files and emails from being used in responses**. Condition: sensitivity label only. Action: prevents item content from being used in the response, though the item may still appear as a citation. Now GA (MC1105017, late June–July 2025).

A default policy is provided: **"Default DLP policy – Protect sensitive M365 Copilot interactions"** ([learn.microsoft.com/.../dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-default-policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-default-policy)). It ships in **simulation mode** with policy tips enabled. It must be moved out of simulation to enforce.

### Implementation steps
1. Verify licensing: Microsoft 365 Copilot license (free or paid), Purview E1/E3/E5 (depending on plan) per the location's licensing rules.
2. In the Purview portal, create a custom DLP policy using the **"Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat"** policy location (note: this disables all other locations for that policy).
3. Add a rule for **sensitivity labels**: condition "Content contains sensitivity label" → "Highly Confidential" / "Top Secret" (or your highest-classification label), action "Restrict access or encrypt the content in Microsoft 365" with "Prevent Copilot from processing content" (or the equivalent Copilot-specific action).
4. Add a separate rule for **SITs**: condition "Content contains sensitive information types" (credit card, SSN, passport, custom SITs), action "Prevent Copilot from processing content → Processing prompts". Move policy out of simulation mode to enforce.
5. (Optional) Add a third rule for external web search: action "Prevent Copilot from processing content → Performing Web Searches".
6. Configure user/group scope and policy tips/overrides.
7. Allow up to 4 hours for Copilot to receive the updated policy.
8. Monitor DLP alerts and Activity Explorer.

### Trade-offs and limitations (Copilot DLP)
- Only covers Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, and pre-built agents that are routed through the same Copilot experience. **It does not cover ChatGPT Enterprise.**
- The "block sensitive prompts" rule only inspects text typed directly into the prompt, not files uploaded into the prompt and not content from Graph sources. Per Microsoft Q&A responses, this is a known design limitation.
- SIT-based prompt blocking is still in preview and subject to rollout dates.
- The "sensitivity label" rule will not block items that the user has no permission to read in the first place (Copilot already enforces the user's Graph permissions), so this is mostly relevant for items the user *can* read but should not flow to AI.
- Some preview-era limitations: not yet fully implemented in Word, Excel, or PowerPoint embedded Copilot.
- DLP for Copilot does **not** control "Copilot computer use" automated browser/session actions (e.g., Researcher/Computer Use opening Gmail and uploading a file) — that is a separate, largely uncovered scenario.

**Verdict:** If the organization is willing to substitute Copilot for ChatGPT Enterprise for DLP-relevant workloads, this is by far the most mature, native, and complete DLP story. If the requirement is genuinely "DLP for ChatGPT Enterprise", this option is **not applicable** and you should rely on the endpoint, network, and OpenAI-side controls in options 3 and 4.

---

## 3) Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps / CASB and Proxy-Based Controls

Defender for Cloud Apps (MDA, now part of Defender XDR) provides three relevant capabilities, and a fourth via the integrated Purview Network Data Security channel.

### 3a. App discovery, sanctioning, and conditional access
- Cloud app catalog includes 35,000+ apps in the "Generative AI" category, including chatgpt.com entries. Admins can mark ChatGPT Enterprise's consumer counterpart as **Unsanctioned**, which automatically blocks it on Defender for Endpoint–onboarded devices ([learn.microsoft.com/.../answers/.../using-defender-for-cloud-apps-to-control-access-to-generative-ai](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5876601/using-defender-for-cloud-apps-to-control-access-to)).
- For **granular** allow-listing, Defender for Cloud Apps is too coarse; the recommended pattern is to keep unsanctioned and use Microsoft Entra Internet Access to allow specific users/groups.

### 3b. Conditional Access app control (session policies)
Session policies require the app to be on the Defender for Cloud Apps supported list or manually onboarded. Per [learn.microsoft.com/.../defender-cloud-apps/session-policy-aad](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/session-policy-aad) and [apps-manual-onboarding-with-microsoft-entra-id](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/apps-manual-onboarding-with-microsoft-entra-id), the **pre-onboarded apps with full session control** do not include chatgpt.com. Custom SaaS apps can be manually onboarded, but only if they use SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect via Entra ID. ChatGPT Enterprise's web app is a third-party service that does not federate through Entra ID, so the standard Conditional Access app control path is **not applicable** to ChatGPT Enterprise.

In-browser protection with Microsoft Edge for Business is the modernized version of the same proxy model ([learn.microsoft.com/.../defender-cloud-apps/in-browser-protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/in-browser-protection)). It supports **Block/Monitor of file download, file upload, copy/cut/paste, print, malware upload/download** for Edge sessions served by Defender for Cloud Apps. It is scoped to apps already onboarded into Conditional Access app control. For chatgpt.com (consumer), you would need a Conditional Access policy that routes traffic through the session controls enterprise app; the same onboarding gap applies for ChatGPT Enterprise.

### 3c. Purview Network Data Security (via Entra Global Secure Access or third-party SASE)
This is the most reliable Microsoft-supported way to enforce real-time DLP on ChatGPT Enterprise and other AI apps at the network layer ([learn.microsoft.com/.../dlp-network-data-security-learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-network-data-security-learn)).

How it works:
- Microsoft Purview shares DLP and collection policy configuration with a SASE/secure browser solution (Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access, or a non-Microsoft partner in the Security Store).
- The SASE solution monitors network traffic from the endpoint and forwards matching text/file events to Purview for classification in **real time** (DLP path) or asynchronously (collection-only path).
- Four activities are supported: text sent to/shared with cloud or AI app, file uploaded/shared with cloud or AI app, text received from cloud or AI app, file downloaded from cloud or AI app.
- Actions: Audit only and Block.
- Inline evaluation size limits: 4 MB of content for uploadText/downloadText, 3 MB for uploadFile/downloadFile.
- The unmanaged-cloud-apps category covers chatgpt.com. Microsoft's documentation explicitly notes: *"Some unmanaged AI apps like ChatGPT, Runway and Meta AI might intermittently send content in encoded form or through dynamically generated endpoints, which can impact policy enforcement."*

**Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access content policies** ([learn.microsoft.com/.../global-secure-access/how-to-network-content-filtering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-network-content-filtering) and the [tutorial](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/tutorial-internet-access-content-policies)) add two layers:
- **Basic content policy** (GA): block or allow by file MIME type. Works without Purview; example given is to block `.doc`, `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.zip` uploads to `*.oaiusercontent.com` (ChatGPT) and `mail.google.com`.
- **Scan with Purview** (preview): inspect text/file content against Purview classifiers and apply DLP rules. Requires a corresponding Purview DLP policy and TLS inspection.

The full end-to-end Microsoft network DLP path is described in [learn.microsoft.com/.../dlp-create-policy-ai-network-data-security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-create-policy-ai-network-data-security). Required licensing for the Entra path: M365 E7 per-seat, or Purview E5 (or equivalent) + Entra Internet Access. For non-Microsoft SASE: Purview E5 + pay-as-you-go.

**Important caveat about ChatGPT Enterprise specifically:** Microsoft's documentation separates "Enterprise AI apps" (the Purview-managed ChatGPT Enterprise connector path, which is post-hoc, 24-hour delay) from "Other AI apps" / "Unmanaged cloud apps" (where network data security does real-time inline block). Per [accuroai.co/.../copilot-chatgpt-enterprise-together-control-matrix-2026](https://accuroai.co/blog/copilot-chatgpt-enterprise-together-control-matrix-2026) and Microsoft's own Learn page, the inline DLP enforcement paths (Edge for Business inline protection, Endpoint DLP, and Network Data Security) treat chatgpt.com as an **unmanaged cloud app**; they do not differentiate between consumer ChatGPT and ChatGPT Enterprise. So the same block that prevents "paste SSN into consumer ChatGPT" also prevents "paste SSN into ChatGPT Enterprise" — but the policy is written against the chatgpt.com domain, not against the "ChatGPT Enterprise" object.

### 3d. Purview Endpoint DLP
For managed Windows (and macOS, with caveats) devices, Endpoint DLP can block:
- **Paste to supported browsers** (Edge, Chrome with Purview extension, Firefox with Purview extension, Safari) using **Sensitive service domain groups** that you populate with the URLs you want to control ([learn.microsoft.com/.../endpoint-dlp-create-policy-restrict-paste-in-browsers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/endpoint-dlp-create-policy-restrict-paste-in-browsers)).
- **File upload to cloud services / restricted cloud service domains**.
- **Copy to clipboard** with allowed-app filters.

Critical limitations of Endpoint DLP paste/upload detection:
- Only standard SITs that don't require advanced classification. EDM, named entities, trainable classifiers, and credential classifiers **do not** trigger on a paste event even when configured.
- The endpoint agent (Microsoft DLP Service) must be healthy. There are documented cases where a policy that previously blocked uploads to chatgpt.com stops enforcing until the service domain list and policy priority are re-published.
- macOS support is available but lags behind Windows; iOS, Android, and unmanaged/BYOD devices are out of scope (this is the primary gap that Edge for Business inline protection was created to close).

### 3e. Edge for Business inline protection (the new control plane)
Per [learn.microsoft.com/.../dlp-browser-dlp-learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-browser-dlp-learn), [learn.microsoft.com/.../dlp-create-policy-block-to-ai-via-edge](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-create-policy-block-to-ai-via-edge), and the [Microsoft Edge blog](https://blogs.windows.com/msedgedev/2025/03/24/new-advanced-data-protection-for-byod-and-ai-in-edge-for-business/):

- Purview DLP is **built into Edge for Business natively**. The device does **not** need to be onboarded to Endpoint DLP for these inline controls to work.
- It applies to **unmanaged consumer AI apps** by default: ChatGPT, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, with an expanding list ([MC1046161](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1046161), [MC1182684](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1182684), [RM518643](https://mc.merill.net/message/RM518643)).
- Detects and audits/blocks: text typed into a prompt, file uploads, copy/paste, and printing. Policy notifications can redirect blocked users to Microsoft 365 Copilot.
- Works on **managed and unmanaged devices** as long as the user is signed into Edge for Business with Entra ID. Personal profiles and InPrivate inherit policies if the work profile used to open them has the policy applied; the personal profile alone is **not** covered.
- Intune-managed Windows devices get additional Intune policies that block data sharing through other browsers to prevent circumvention. The Edge management service auto-creates these Intune and Edge configuration policies when a Purview DLP policy targeting unmanaged apps is saved.
- Some Edge DLP controls (e.g., session policies for file protection, built-in DLP scanning) still require the reverse proxy rather than the in-browser path.
- For BYOD with Edge for Business, Purview DLP for unmanaged devices is pay-as-you-go.

**Implication for ChatGPT Enterprise specifically:** chatgpt.com is treated as the same target as consumer ChatGPT for these inline controls. If you block "paste SSN to chatgpt.com" via Edge for Business, the user cannot paste it into ChatGPT Enterprise either. But because the policy is domain-based, you cannot say "block SSN for ChatGPT Enterprise but allow it for ChatGPT Plus" — the granularity is at the domain level.

### Implementation steps (layered)
1. **Edge for Business inline protection (first-line, easiest)**
   - Ensure users sign into Edge for Business with Entra ID. Enforce work profile for in-browser protection.
   - In Purview, create a DLP policy with location = "Unmanaged cloud apps" (browser) or use the dedicated "Help prevent sharing via Microsoft Edge for Business to unmanaged AI apps" template.
   - In the rule, use SIT or sensitivity-label conditions and the action "Upload text to AI site" / "Upload file to AI site" set to Block or Audit.
   - Test in simulation, then enforce. Allow the Edge management service to auto-create the supporting Intune/Edge configuration policies.
2. **Endpoint DLP (managed Windows fleet)**
   - Onboard Windows devices to Purview (via Defender for Endpoint onboarding or the MDE client).
   - In Endpoint DLP settings, create a **Sensitive service domain group** containing `chatgpt.com` and `*.chatgpt.com` (also `*.oaiusercontent.com` for ChatGPT response viewing).
   - Create a DLP policy with location = Devices. Add rules with SIT/sensitivity-label conditions and actions "Paste to supported browsers" = Block, and "Upload to restricted cloud service domains" = Block. Use exceptions for approved internal domains.
   - Use the Antimalware Client version ≥ 4.18.23110 and the latest Edge/Chrome/Firefox extensions.
3. **Entra Global Secure Access + Purview Network Data Security (broadest cross-app)**
   - Enable the Internet Access traffic forwarding profile in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
   - Install the Global Secure Access client on Entra-joined devices.
   - Configure a TLS inspection policy (required to inspect encrypted AI traffic).
   - Create a content policy: target FQDNs `*.oaiusercontent.com` and `*.chatgpt.com` (or use the "Generative AI" adaptive app scope), action = Block on Upload, with optional "Scan with Purview" to enable content inspection.
   - In Purview, create a DLP policy with the **Network data security** location and the same SITs/labels as the endpoint policy. Use action = Block.
   - Create a separate collection policy for the "DSPM for AI – Detect sensitive info shared with AI via network" recommendation for visibility.
4. **Defender for Cloud Apps (discovery + governance)**
   - In the cloud app catalog, mark consumer chatgpt.com as **Unsanctioned** if you want a hard block on consumer ChatGPT for everyone.
   - Use Entra Internet Access for exception allow-listing for specific users/groups that need ChatGPT.
   - (Optional) Create an app governance policy with `Category equals Generative AI AND Tag equals Unsanctioned` for continuous reporting.

### Trade-offs and limitations
- **Defender for Cloud Apps session policies** (the classic proxy model) do **not** natively cover ChatGPT Enterprise because ChatGPT Enterprise does not federate through Entra ID, so the Conditional Access app control redirect cannot be enforced. You can route chatgpt.com generically, but you will also be routing the consumer version through the proxy and will incur the same proxy limitations.
- **Endpoint DLP** only works on onboarded Windows (and macOS, lagging) devices. iOS, Android, and BYOD are not protected unless you pair with Edge for Business.
- **Edge for Business inline protection** is the most elegant option but is **scoped to Edge**. A user on Chrome or Firefox on a BYOD device has no inline protection unless you also deploy the Purview browser extension on Chrome/Firefox.
- **Network Data Security** has a 4 MB inline text / 3 MB file limit. Larger uploads are not evaluated.
- **ChatGPT-specific gotcha** (per Microsoft): *"Some unmanaged AI apps like ChatGPT, Runway and Meta AI might intermittently send content in encoded form or through dynamically generated endpoints, which can impact policy enforcement."* — meaning the DLP path can be bypassed by some interactions even with the policy configured.
- The proxy and in-browser session controls do not protect content that the user types in the prompt field (file upload and copy/paste are covered, but free-text typing is the gap that Edge for Business inline protection was built to close).
- Latency between policy changes and enforcement can be 30 minutes to several hours; for the Copilot location, Microsoft quotes up to 4 hours.
- TLS inspection is required for the SASE network DLP path; it may be incompatible with some certificate-pinned apps, and there is a known limitation that Google Workspace in Enterprise Edge is not supported for in-browser protection and falls back to the reverse proxy.

---

## 4) ChatGPT Enterprise Admin / Settings and API-Side Controls

This option is the OpenAI-side counterpart and the only layer that is fully under OpenAI's control. It is not "DLP" in the Microsoft Purview sense, but it is part of the overall DLP posture and is the layer that Purview's connector ultimately reads from.

Sources: [openai.com/business-data](https://openai.com/business-data/), [help.openai.com/.../data-residency-and-inference-residency-for-chatgpt](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9903489-data-residency-and-inference-residency-for-chatgpt), [help.openai.com/.../managing-admin-keys-in-admin-console](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001407), [help.openai.com/.../managing-workspace-settings-in-chatgpt-enterprise](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8411955-managing-workspace-settings-in-chatgpt-enterprise), [learn.chatgpt.com/.../enterprise/admin-setup.md](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/admin-setup.md), [learn.chatgpt.com/.../enterprise/governance.md](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/governance.md), and [help.openai.com/.../openai-compliance-platform-for-enterprise-and-edu-customers](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9261474-openai-compliance-platform-for-enterprise-and-edu-customers).

### Native controls available

| Control | What it does | DLP relevance |
|---|---|---|
| **Compliance Platform / Compliance Logs Platform** (immutable, append-only JSONL logs; 30-day retention; export to SIEM/DLP/eDiscovery) | Provides audit, authentication, app, and conversation-message logs. Conversation message access requires workspace-owner approval. | Provides the **data source** for the Purview connector. This is where the 24-hour ingestion delay originates. |
| **Stateful Compliance API** (query state at a point in time) | Admin API for users, projects, invites, audit logs, etc. | Useful for incident response and reconciliation, not real-time blocking. |
| **Admin Keys (Admin Console)** | Scoped API keys with permissions per category (Apps, Users, Group Management, Compliance, etc.). Broad compliance and Conversation messages require workspace owner. | The mechanism to grant Microsoft Purview read access to ChatGPT Enterprise. |
| **SCIM provisioning** | Sync user/group lifecycle from Entra ID (or other IdP) to ChatGPT Enterprise. | Reduces orphan accounts; quick offboarding is part of DLP. |
| **SSO via SAML** with Entra ID | Federated identity. | Enables Entra-based Conditional Access to gate the chatgpt.com sign-in. |
| **IP allowlists** | Restrict access to corporate ranges. | Reduces the attack surface; forces access through corporate egress where Endpoint DLP/Network Data Security applies. |
| **Data residency** (US, EU, UK, JP, CA, KR, SG, AU, IN, UAE at-rest) and **inference residency** (US, EU) | Confines customer content at rest, and optionally inference, to a region. | Compliance benefit; not DLP in the data-leak sense. |
| **Zero Data Retention (ZDR)** for the API platform; configurable retention for Enterprise. | Controls how long OpenAI retains business data. | Reduces the data-at-rest exposure window at the OpenAI side. |
| **Enterprise Key Management (EKM)** | Customer-controlled encryption keys for stored data. | Stronger at-rest protection; does not prevent in-flight leakage. |
| **Workspace settings**: defaults, allowed domains for connectors, custom GPT governance, apps allow-list, GPT/connector approvals, sharing controls | Constrains which tools and connectors members can use. | Constrains exfiltration paths; complementary to DLP. |
| **Agent Security** (orchestrator controls, approval requirements, allowed web search modes, managed tool controls, sandboxing, filesystem permissions, network controls) | Workspace policy plane. | Limits what agents can do once invoked. |
| **Audit events** in Admin Console + Compliance API | Who did what when. | After-the-fact DLP signal. |

### Implementation steps
1. **Identity and access**: configure SSO with Entra ID and verified domains; enable SCIM provisioning. Decide default seat types and group mapping.
2. **Admin keys**: workspace owner creates one Admin key with the read scope for compliance, stored in Azure Key Vault for the Purview connector; create a separate key for the SIEM ingestion pipeline.
3. **Compliance platform export**: build a continuous downloader against the Compliance Logs Platform for all relevant log categories (audit, authentication, conversation messages if you have owner approval). 30-day window; **you must export continuously** if you need longer retention.
4. **Workspace defaults**: set the default model, default new-chat behavior, member cost visibility, and seat defaults. Set the model and feature defaults so that "Work" and "Codex" features are enabled/disabled per your policy.
5. **Apps and connectors**: explicitly allow-list connectors and external apps; enable admin approval for GPTs and connectors per workspace policy.
6. **Data residency and inference residency**: enable both at the workspace level; check that your supported region is the one your data sovereignty regime requires.
7. **Data retention**: enable the retention controls available to your plan; if ZDR is available and you need it, opt in (subject to plan/region eligibility).
8. **EKM**: enable Enterprise Key Management if your plan supports it; rotate keys per your key-management policy.
9. **IP allowlist**: restrict to corporate egress so that the chatgpt.com sessions transit your SASE / Endpoint DLP / Edge for Business inline protection paths.
10. **Agent Security policies**: configure approval requirements, managed tool controls, sandboxing, and execution network controls. Configure Codex Cloud and Local computer access policies for the relevant teams.
11. **Audit log review**: subscribe to audit and authentication log alerts in your SIEM; build insider-risk correlation with Entra ID sign-in risk.

### Trade-offs and limitations
- **No native in-product, inline DLP on the prompt at the OpenAI layer.** OpenAI does not offer "Purview-style" prompt-time policy enforcement on the ChatGPT Enterprise side. The workspace controls are governance and policy, not data-in-motion blocking.
- **24-hour latency** for OpenAI's Compliance Platform logs; for the Purview connector, this is in addition to Purview's own processing time. Real-time blocking is not possible from this side.
- **30-day retention** on the Compliance Logs Platform; deleted data is not recoverable from OpenAI. You must continuously export.
- **No sensitivity-label awareness** in OpenAI's pipeline. Sensitivity labels (MIP/AIP) cannot be passed to ChatGPT Enterprise, and ChatGPT Enterprise cannot read MIP-encrypted content. This means a Purview label-based DLP rule that relies on encrypted content will see no content, which is good for confidentiality, but it also means OpenAI-side controls cannot honor those labels.
- **Conversation message access** requires a workspace owner; admins cannot self-grant this. If the Compliance Officer is not the workspace owner, you need an admin key workflow that involves the owner.
- **EKM, residency, and ZDR** are subject to plan/region/feature eligibility and may exclude certain features (e.g., Work with UAE inference residency is not supported, per the OpenAI admin docs).
- **Agent Security / managed tool controls** are effective but require careful policy design; misconfiguration can break legitimate workflows.
- **No DLP enforcement** for content **typed** into the prompt in the ChatGPT Enterprise web UI; the only signal is the post-hoc compliance log. This is the gap that must be closed by Endpoint DLP / Edge for Business / Network Data Security on the Microsoft side.

---

## Recommended Configuration for a Corporate Environment

A single control will not deliver "true DLP" for ChatGPT Enterprise. The recommended posture is a layered one that puts **the actual block as close to the user as possible**, with **OpenAI-side controls** providing governance, residency, and audit, and **Purview** providing central reporting.

### Tier 1 — Inline prevention (where the data can actually be stopped)
1. **Edge for Business inline protection (Purview DLP) — primary on managed Windows + BYOD-with-Edge**
   - Target: chatgpt.com and *.oaiusercontent.com via the "unmanaged AI app" pattern.
   - Block typing into the prompt, file upload, copy/paste, and printing when the content contains SITs or sensitivity labels.
   - Pair with Intune-managed Windows + Edge work profile enforcement to prevent browser circumvention.
2. **Purview Endpoint DLP — primary on Intune-managed Windows fleet**
   - Sensitive service domain group containing chatgpt.com, *.chatgpt.com, *.oaiusercontent.com.
   - Block "Paste to supported browsers" and "Upload to restricted cloud service domains" for SITs and sensitivity labels.
   - Provide a "Block with override" policy tip for education-first mode.
3. **Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access + Purview Network Data Security — primary on Entra-joined devices that may use Chrome, Firefox, Office add-ins, or local AI clients**
   - TLS inspection enabled.
   - Content policy: block text and file uploads to chatgpt.com and *.oaiusercontent.com; "Scan with Purview" for content-aware blocking.
   - Mirror the same SIT/label rules in the Purview DLP policy with the Network data security location.
4. **Defender for Cloud Apps** — discovery, sanctioning, and continuous reporting for Generative AI category. Use to identify residual unsanctioned AI usage and feed app governance alerts.

### Tier 2 — OpenAI-side governance
5. **ChatGPT Enterprise workspace hardening**: SSO via Entra ID, SCIM, IP allowlist to corporate ranges, EKM, residency, ZDR where eligible.
6. **Agent Security / workspace policy**: approval requirements, allowed web search modes, managed tool controls, connector allow-listing, custom GPT governance.
7. **Admin keys + Compliance Platform export**: continuous export of audit, authentication, app, and conversation-message logs to a SIEM; 30-day window respected.

### Tier 3 — Purview governance and audit (the connector is not prevention)
8. **Purview ChatGPT Enterprise connector** for after-the-fact classification, retention, eDiscovery, insider risk, and communication compliance.
9. **DSPM for AI** reports filtered to "Enterprise AI apps / ChatGPT Enterprise" for monthly posture review.
10. **Insider Risk Management "Risky AI usage" policy** + **Communication Compliance** policy to surface risky prompts from the captured data.

### Tier 4 — Substitute where appropriate
11. For workloads where the user has a meaningful choice between ChatGPT Enterprise and Copilot, consider routing DLP-sensitive workflows to **Microsoft 365 Copilot + Purview DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot location**, which provides native prompt-time blocking that no other layer can match.

### Key trade-offs at the architecture level
- The 24-hour ingestion delay of the Purview ChatGPT Enterprise connector means it cannot be in the prevention path. It is acceptable for governance and audit, not for incident response.
- Sensitivity labels are not honored by ChatGPT Enterprise. DLP rules that rely on label-based content inspection will not see content encrypted with MIP; the encryption itself is the protection.
- ChatGPT Enterprise cannot be differentiated from consumer ChatGPT by any of the inline controls (Edge, Endpoint DLP, Network Data Security). All of them are domain-based. If you have a "block consumer ChatGPT but allow ChatGPT Enterprise" rule, you must enforce it at the network or Edge level using the consumer-specific domain entries.
- The only way to get true prompt-time DLP for AI assistants in the Microsoft stack is to use Microsoft 365 Copilot with the DLP for Copilot location. That is not "DLP for ChatGPT Enterprise", it is DLP for Copilot. The two products serve different use cases; running both is a common enterprise pattern.

### Known limitations summary (applies to all options)
- **No native prompt-time DLP for ChatGPT Enterprise.** The Purview connector is post-hoc and 24 hours delayed.
- **Sensitivity labels are not supported** on the ChatGPT Enterprise path.
- **Inline evaluation is bounded**: 4 MB text, 3 MB file for Network Data Security; only standard SITs for Endpoint DLP paste.
- **Device coverage gaps**: Endpoint DLP requires Windows (macOS lags; iOS/Android/BYOD unsupported unless paired with Edge for Business).
- **Browser coverage gaps**: Edge for Business inline protection only works in Edge; Chrome/Firefox require the Purview extension on Windows.
- **OpenAI-side enforcement gap**: OpenAI does not provide inline DLP on prompts; their controls are governance and audit.
- **Proxy session controls** in Defender for Cloud Apps do not natively onboard ChatGPT Enterprise because the app is not Entra-ID-federated.
- **TLS inspection is required** for Network Data Security content inspection and can break certificate-pinned apps.
- **Preview/GA timing**: several of the strongest controls (DLP for Copilot prompt blocking, Scan with Purview, certain Edge for Business protections) are still in preview or recently GA as of late 2025/early 2026; verify current status in the Microsoft 365 Message Center before relying on them in production.

### Bottom line
- For "DLP for ChatGPT Enterprise" as a literal product question: there is **no native Purview DLP for ChatGPT Enterprise**. Use the **layered model above** with Edge for Business inline protection + Endpoint DLP + Entra Global Secure Access + Purview Network Data Security as the prevention stack, and the Purview ChatGPT Enterprise connector as the audit/governance layer.
- For "DLP for an AI assistant integrated with Microsoft Purview" generally: **Copilot for Microsoft 365 + Purview DLP for the Microsoft 365 Copilot location** is the only Microsoft-native option that delivers true prompt-time DLP, and it is the recommended path for any workload where the user can choose the assistant.

# Technical Analysis of Competing Digital Identity Standards

## 1. Executive Summary

This report compares six identity systems spanning three architectural philosophies: decentralized (W3C DIDs/VCs), federated/strong-authentication (FIDO2/WebAuthn), and state-issued foundational IDs (EU eIDAS 2.0/EUDI Wallet, India Aadhaar, Estonia e-Residency). Each makes distinct trade-offs among privacy, interoperability, surveillance resistance, credential recovery, and use-case fit. No single system dominates across all dimensions; selection is largely a function of the deployment context, the identity-assurance level required, and the regulatory environment.

## 2. Technical Foundations of Each System

### 2.1 W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0

A DID is a URI with the scheme `did:` followed by a method identifier and a method-specific unique string, defined in [W3C DID v1.0 Recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/did-1.0/). The specification "does not presuppose any particular technology or cryptography to underpin the generation, persistence, resolution, or interpretation of DIDs," allowing DIDs to be anchored on distributed ledgers, decentralized file systems, peer-to-peer networks, or even federated/centralized systems ([DID v1.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/did/)). The current 1.1 working draft is at Candidate Recommendation stage ([DID v1.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/did-1.1/)).

A DID resolves to a DID document containing the eight core properties: `id` (required), `alsoKnownAs`, `controller`, `verificationMethod`, `authentication`, `assertionMethod`, `keyAgreement`, `capabilityInvocation`, `capabilityDelegation`, and `service` ([DID v1.0 §5 Core Properties](https://www.w3.org/TR/did-1.0/)). The document is "a serialization of the data model" and "typically contains cryptographic material that enables authentication of the DID subject" ([DID v1.0 (2019 draft)](https://www.w3.org/TR/2019/WD-did-core-20191127/)). DIDs deliberately separate the *identifier* from any *verifiable data registry*, so method choice is independent of identifier format.

The W3C [DID Method Rubric v2.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/did-rubric/) catalogs a wide and heterogeneous method ecosystem: `did:key` (pure self-contained keypair, no registry), `did:web` (DNS-based, traditional web hosting), `did:ion` (Bitcoin + IPFS), `did:btcr` (Bitcoin), `did:ethr` (Ethereum smart contracts), `did:indy` (Hyperledger Indy, supersedes `did:sov`), `did:git`, and `did:hedera`, among others.

### 2.2 W3C Verifiable Credentials (VCs) 2.0

VCs implement an "extensible data model … for the exchange of these credentials that is composed of issuers, holders, and verifiers" ([VC 2.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/)). A conforming VC is a compacted JSON-LD document with media type `application/vc` (or `application/vp` for presentations) and "MUST be secured by at least one securing mechanism" such as a Data Integrity proof or a JWS-based envelope ([VC 2.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/)).

The data model separates the credential's structural integrity (cryptographic) from its semantic content (claims), allowing revocation, expiration, and selective disclosure patterns. The [W3C VC Use Cases document](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-use-cases/) describes healthcare scenarios including physician licensure verification, online pharmacy validation, insurance claims, and cross-border "traveling illness" presentation.

### 2.3 FIDO2 / WebAuthn

WebAuthn (W3C) combined with CTAP2 (FIDO Alliance) forms FIDO2. The [WebAuthn Level 2 specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/) defines an API "enabling the creation and use of strong, attested, scoped, public key-based credentials by web applications, for the purpose of strongly authenticating users." Registration creates a public key credential on an authenticator; later authentication is a challenge–response in which the server checks a signature.

Three structural properties differentiate FIDO2 from a generic public-key system:
1. **Relying Party scoping.** "A public key credential … can only be accessed by origins belonging to that Relying Party. This scoping is enforced jointly by conforming User Agents and authenticators" ([WebAuthn L2](https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/)).
2. **Cross-RP privacy.** "Relying Parties are not able to detect any properties, or even the existence, of credentials scoped to other Relying Parties" ([WebAuthn L2](https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/)).
3. **Attestation.** "Authenticators provide cryptographic proof of their properties to Relying Parties via attestation" ([WebAuthn L2](https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/)).

FIDO2 is fundamentally an **authentication** protocol, not an identity-issuance or attribute-credential system. CTAP2 is the [Client-to-Authenticator Protocol](https://fidoalliance.org/specs/fido-v2.3-rd-20251023/fido-client-to-authenticator-protocol-v2.3-rd-20251023.pdf) for roaming authenticators (USB/NFC/BLE). The 2025 paper [Privacy and Security of FIDO2 Revisited (IACR ePrint 2025/459)](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/459.pdf) notes that "WebAuthn provides user privacy" under the Hanzlik et al. unlinkability definition for non-resident keys, with extensions by Bindel et al. for resident keys and attestation.

### 2.4 EU eIDAS 2.0 / European Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI)

The framework is established by [Regulation (EU) 2024/1183](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1183/oj), amending the original eIDAS Regulation 910/2014. Member States must provide an EU Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI Wallet) to all natural and legal persons by end of 2026 ([eIDAS 2.0 summary](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/EN/legal-content/summary/the-establishment-of-the-european-digital-identity-framework-including-the-provision-of-european-digital-identity-wallets-and-trust-services.html?fromSummary=31)).

Four implementing regulations were adopted on 28 November 2024:
- [CIR 2024/2977](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2024/2977/oj/eng): person identification data (PID) and electronic attestations of attributes (EAAs)
- [CIR 2024/2979](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ%3AL_202402979): wallet integrity and core functionalities
- [CIR 2024/2980](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/main/docs/architecture-and-reference-framework-main.md): ecosystem notifications
- [CIR 2024/2981](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ:L_202402981): certification of Wallet Solutions
- [CIR 2024/2982](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/main/docs/architecture-and-reference-framework-main.md): protocols and interfaces

The technical reference is the [Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF) v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0), which defines wallet components, lifecycle, presentation flows (proximity and remote), Wallet Secure Cryptographic Devices (WSCD), and pseudonym generation. Privacy is built around selective disclosure: Recital 59 defines it as "a concept empowering the owner of data to disclose only certain parts of a larger data set." Two technical mechanisms are specified:
- **[RFC 9901 SD-JWT](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9901)**: salted-hash selective disclosure for JSON Web Tokens.
- **[TS4-ZKP / TS14 Multi-Message Signatures](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-standards-and-technical-specifications/blob/main/docs/technical-specifications/ts4-zkp.md)**: BBS+ signatures allowing zero-knowledge proof that a hidden set of attributes was signed by the issuer. The ZKP discussion topic states current ZKP approaches "cannot be deemed fully suitable or mature enough for direct integration" but member states "should integrate different privacy-preserving technologies, such as zero knowledge proof" ([ARF Topic G](https://eu-digital-identity-wallet.github.io/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/2.7.3/discussion-topics/g-zero-knowledge-proof/)).

### 2.5 India Aadhaar

Aadhaar is the world's largest biometric ID system. Per the [UIDAI Annual Report 2024-25](https://uidai.gov.in/images/E_UIDAI_Annual_Report_24-25.pdf), "more than 141.80 crore Aadhaar numbers have been generated and issued to the residents of India till 31st March 2025" (1.418 billion). The October 2024 [Aadhaar Saturation Report](https://uidai.gov.in/images/Aadhaar_Saturation_Report_31102024.pdf) shows national penetration of 95.03% (live Aadhaar vs. projected 2024 population of ~1.40 billion).

Architecturally:
- **Central Identities Data Repository (CIDR)** is defined in the [Aadhaar (Data Security) Regulations, 2016](https://www.uidai.gov.in/images/The_Aadhaar_Data_Security_Regulations_2016.pdf) as "a centralised database in one or more locations containing all Aadhaar numbers issued to Aadhaar number holders along with the corresponding demographic information and biometric information."
- The [Aadhaar Authentication API 1.6](https://uidai.gov.in/images/resource/aadhaar_authentication_api_2_5.pdf) supports a 12-digit Aadhaar number, a revocable 16-digit **Virtual ID (VID)**, or a **UID Token**, with biometrics (fingerprints, iris, face) or demographic factors. Responses are "yes/no" only.
- **[UIDAI Circular 14 of 2025](https://uidai.gov.in/images/Circular-No.14_of-2025.pdf)** mandates an **Aadhaar Data Vault (ADV)** for any entity that holds Aadhaar numbers, with HSM-based encryption, and prohibits storage of Aadhaar numbers in non-ADV systems.
- The de-duplication and authentication infrastructure is built on proprietary biometric SDKs from L-1 Identity Solutions and Morpho S.A.S., which "cannot be independently audited" ([Aadhaar technical critique filed in Supreme Court](https://www.scobserver.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Technical-Standpoint-of-Aadhaar-Sibal-7-02-2018.pdf)).

### 2.6 Estonia e-Residency

Estonia runs one of the most mature state-issued eID systems. Per the [e-Residency dashboard](https://www.e-resident.gov.ee/dashboard/), the program has issued 144,000+ e-resident digital IDs across 185 nationalities since launch on 1 December 2014. The 2024 figures ([Baltic Times 2024 report](https://www.baltictimes.com/new_milestone_for_e-residency-with_record_number_of_companies_founded_in_2024/), [Invest in Estonia 2024](https://investinestonia.com/estonian-e-residency-attracts-record-interest-and-revenue-in-2024/)) show:
- 11,484 new e-residents in 2024 (+5% YoY)
- 4,818 new companies founded by e-residents in 2024 (record)
- €66.8 million in state tax revenue and fees in 2024
- ~1 in 5 new Estonian companies in 2024 had an e-resident founder

The technical substrate is described in the [RIA Estonian eID ecosystem document (October 2025)](https://www.ria.ee/sites/default/files/documents/2025-10/Estonian-eID-ecosystem.pdf) and [Privacy International's e-Estonia case study](https://privacyinternational.org/case-study/4737/id-systems-analysed-e-estonia):
- **PKI-based.** "All widely used eID means are based on PKI" (ID-card, Mobile-ID, Digital ID, e-Resident's digital ID, Diplomatic ID, Residence permit card). The certification service is operated by private partner SK ID Solutions AS under state oversight.
- **X-Road (X-tee).** A free open-source data-exchange layer (MIT license on GitHub) connecting the Population Register, Land Register, Commercial Register, etc. via "Central Services, Security Servers, Information Systems, Time-Stamping Authority(ies), and Certificate Authorities" ([X-Road paper](https://cyber.ee/uploads/T_4_1_X_Road_complete_solution_for_inter_organizational_information_exchange_bf61cb2da1.pdf)).
- **KSI Blockchain.** Estonia deployed Guardtime's Keyless Signature Infrastructure for data integrity after the 2007 cyberattacks ([Interoperable Europe case study](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/public-sector-tech-watch/use-national-blockchain-infrastructure-support-e-residency-initiative-estonia)).
- **Data embassies.** "Data held by the Estonian government is decentralised and duplicated through the use of data embassies … despite sitting outside Estonia's borders, [they] remain fully under Estonia's control and have the same rights as physical embassies such as immunity" ([Privacy International](https://privacyinternational.org/case-study/4737/id-systems-analysed-e-estonia)).

The e-Residency program itself, however, has faced independent scrutiny: a 2024 [ERR News investigation](https://news.err.ee/1609279218/estonian-e-residency-success-metrics-impossible-to-verify) reported that EISA's claimed revenue figures "cannot be verified" because the Tax Board "does not allow for it to be verified" and "which companies are involved and what exactly is considered in this revenue calculation is not known by the e-residency team."

## 3. Comparative Analysis

### 3.1 Privacy

| System | Privacy architecture | Key mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| W3C DIDs/VCs | Privacy by design, no central registry requirement | Cryptographically bound, peer-to-peer presentation; minimal disclosure; ZKP-capable |
| FIDO2/WebAuthn | Strong authentication privacy | RP-scoped credentials (no cross-site tracking); Hanzlik et al. unlinkability for non-resident keys |
| EUDI Wallet | Selective disclosure mandated by regulation | SD-JWT (RFC 9901) and BBS+ ZKP per [ARF Topic G](https://eu-digital-identity-wallet.github.io/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/2.7.3/discussion-topics/g-zero-knowledge-proof/) |
| Aadhaar | Centralised biometrics; VID as privacy mitigation | [Aadhaar Authentication API 1.6](https://uidai.gov.in/images/resource/aadhaar_authentication_api_2_5.pdf) returns only yes/no; Virtual ID is "a fungible number mapped to Aadhaar Number" |
| Estonia eID | PKI with strong separation; transaction signing | Each authentication is signed; X-Road logs every query |

W3C VCs and EUDI Wallet are explicitly engineered for data minimisation. The [VC 2.0 specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/) describes a holder presenting only the subset of claims required ("a credential is a set of one or more claims made by the same entity … a verifiable credential is a set of tamper-evident claims and metadata that cryptographically prove who issued it"). EUDI's Recital 14 requires ZKP so the verifier learns only that a statement is true ([ARF Topic G](https://eu-digital-identity-wallet.github.io/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/2.7.3/discussion-topics/g-zero-knowledge-proof/)).

FIDO2's privacy is high *between* relying parties ("Relying Parties are not able to detect any properties, or even the existence, of credentials scoped to other Relying Parties," [WebAuthn L2](https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/)) but it reveals authentication events to the relying party on every login. It carries no attribute privacy because it is not a credential system.

Aadhaar and Estonia represent the centralisation trade-off. Aadhaar's CIDR is, per the [RBI report quoted in the Supreme Court filing](https://www.scobserver.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Technical-Standpoint-of-Aadhaar-Sibal-7-02-2018.pdf), "a single target … for cyber criminals as well as India's external enemies," and the de-duplication algorithm "traverses the full database." The Virtual ID (16-digit) and UID Token mitigations reduce correlation, but biometric data is held centrally and is the ultimate identity anchor.

Estonia's privacy posture is structurally similar to Aadhaar in that a central Population Register is the canonical source, but X-Road logs every cross-agency query, which creates an audit trail *and* a surveillance target. The privacy model is "trust the state" plus cryptographic accountability.

### 3.2 Interoperability

Interoperability is the dimension with the widest variance:

- **W3C DIDs/VCs.** Theoretically maximal but in practice fragmented. The [DID Implementation Guide v1.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/2021/NOTE-did-imp-guide-20211012/) notes "There are several 'families' of DID methods, including Hyperledger Indy, Sidetree, and various methods that share similar smart contracts." The [DID Method Rubric](https://www.w3.org/TR/did-rubric/) grades interoperability A (any wallet, any resolver, any registry) through D (single combined suite). `did:web` and `did:key` score well; method-specific chains (Indy, ION) do not. Interoperability test reports such as [did:key Interoperability Report 1.0](https://w3c-ccg.github.io/did-key-test-suite/) show multiple implementations still fail mandatory assertions (e.g., raising `methodNotSupported` errors).
- **FIDO2/WebAuthn.** Highest real-world interoperability among the technical standards. WebAuthn is a W3C Recommendation; CTAP2 is a FIDO Alliance Proposed Standard. Browser and platform support is near-universal. Limitation: an RP cannot share a credential across distinct second-level domains; the [Related Origin Requests explainer](https://github.com/w3c/webauthn/blob/main/explainers/related-origin-requests.md) describes workarounds using redirects and iframes.
- **EUDI Wallet.** Interoperability is the explicit design goal. The [EUDI Wallet Toolbox](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/eudi-wallet-toolbox) is mandated by the [Commission Recommendation 2021/946](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/main/docs/architecture-and-reference-framework-main.md) and is being implemented through [Implementing Regulation 2024/2982 (protocols and interfaces)](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/main/docs/architecture-and-reference-framework-main.md). However, mandatory rollout is by end of 2026; cross-border interoperability between Member State wallets is not yet proven.
- **Aadhaar.** Interoperable across India for any entity registered as a "Requesting Entity" with UIDAI, but has no interoperability with foreign identity systems by design. The [Authentication API 1.6](https://uidai.gov.in/images/resource/aadhaar_authentication_api_2_5.pdf) is private and not international.
- **Estonia eID/e-Residency.** Interoperable across the Estonian public and private sector via X-Road. The [RIA ecosystem document](https://www.ria.ee/sites/default/files/documents/2025-10/Estonian-eID-ecosystem.pdf) details the normative background of legal acts, technical interoperability standards, and certifying requirements. Interoperability is bounded by Estonia's national scope; the e-Residency card is a national ID for *digital* purposes, not a travel document.

### 3.3 Resistance to Surveillance

This is the dimension where the systems differ most starkly.

**W3C DIDs/VCs.** Architecturally the strongest. Because DIDs "can be created based on identifiers registered in federated or centralized identity management systems" but are not *required* to use such systems ([DID v1.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/did-1.0/)), the holder can choose a method that avoids any surveillance-prone infrastructure. The W3C's design principles explicitly include portability, privacy, and minimal disclosure. Holders do not need to query any third party to prove a credential; the verifier checks the issuer's signature directly.

**FIDO2/WebAuthn.** Resistant to cross-site tracking at the protocol level (RP-scoped credentials) but every authentication is logged by the relying party. FIDO2 is not designed to hide the fact of a login from a server.

**EUDI Wallet.** Designed to minimise issuer/verifier correlation. [ARF §5a(23) requirements](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/eudi-wallet-toolbox) (in implementing regulations) require that wallet presentations "not allow providers of electronic attestations of attributes or any other party, after the issuance of the attestation of attributes, to obtain data that allows transactions or user behaviour to be tracked, linked or correlated." However, the legal framework is the [eIDAS Regulation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2014/910/oj) requiring relying parties in some cases to identify users (e.g., regulated services), which limits privacy in practice.

**Aadhaar.** Architecturally the most surveillance-prone. The Supreme Court of India considered and largely rejected the "surveillance state" argument in the [Puttaswamy / Aadhaar judgment of September 2018](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2012/35071/35071_2012_Judgement_26-Sep-2018.pdf). The 4-1 majority held that "the architecture of Aadhaar as well as the provisions of the Aadhaar Act do not tend to create a surveillance state." Justice D.Y. Chandrachud's dissent characterised Aadhaar as unconstitutional, and the majority nonetheless struck down parts of Section 57 (allowing private entities to seek authentication) as disproportionate, and barred storage of authentication data for more than six months ([Indian Express summary](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/supreme-court-aadhaar-verdict-some-right-to-privacy-5376298/)).

A serious 2024 incident illustrated real-world exposure: Resecurity reported an [815 million-record breach of Indian resident Aadhaar & Passport data](https://coercioncode.com/2024/04/12/the-worlds-largest-biometric-digital-id-system-indias-aadhaar-is-hacked-nearly-10-of-the-world-population/) advertised on Breach Forums (October 2023; reported in 2024) — roughly 60% of the enrolled Indian population.

**Estonia eID.** PKI is well-instrumented. X-Road timestamps and signs every inter-institutional query ([X-Road paper](https://cyber.ee/uploads/T_4_1_X_Road_complete_solution_for_inter_organizational_information_exchange_bf61cb2da1.pdf)), creating an audit trail rather than a surveillance vacuum, but the centralised Population Register remains a single point of access. KSI blockchain provides integrity but not access control.

### 3.4 Recovery Mechanisms for Lost Credentials

| System | Native recovery | Weakness / gap |
|---|---|---|
| W3C DIDs/VCs | No standard recovery in [DID Core v1.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/did-1.0/); ad-hoc per method | Key loss → permanent loss unless method supports rotation |
| FIDO2/WebAuthn | Re-registration, account recovery codes, multi-device sync (passkeys) | Roaming hardware authenticator loss is catastrophic without backup |
| EUDI Wallet | Wallet recovery is a regulated topic; member-state implementation | Recovery = identity-reissuance; standards still maturing |
| Aadhaar | Re-authentication via VID + biometric at any Aadhaar centre | Requires physical/biometric verification |
| Estonia eID | Re-issuance via Police and Border Guard Board | Requires in-person verification |

For W3C DIDs, the absence of standard recovery is acknowledged as a barrier. The [W3C-CCG DID-RECOVERY draft](https://github.com/w3c-ccg/did-recovery) and the [DID Key Recovery Extension (DID-KR) by Sirraya Labs](https://github.com/sirraya-labs/did-kr) propose three complementary mechanisms:
- **Type A — Social ZKP Recovery:** threshold guardians using Feldman Verifiable Secret Sharing with Schnorr proofs.
- **Type B — Deterministic Seedling:** hierarchical deterministic (HD) keys with Verifiable Delay Function (VDF) time-locks for inheritance scenarios.
- **Type C — MPC-Mediated:** fROST threshold signatures with proactive share refreshment.

The Ethereum-aligned [EIP-7093: Social Recovery Interface](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7093) formalises guardian-based recovery for smart contract accounts. Recovery periods in deployed systems range from 36 hours (Argent) to 14 days (Candide Safe module) per the [Ethereum IPTF pattern](https://github.com/ethereum/iptf-map/blob/master/patterns/pattern-social-recovery.md). For stateless or low-trust populations, however, social recovery requires a guardian set, which may not exist.

FIDO2's modern form (passkeys with cloud sync via Apple, Google, Microsoft, or password managers) provides robust recovery in the consumer case, but a hardware-token-only deployment without backup has zero recovery. A 2018 paper [A Tour of WebAuthn](https://www.imperialviolet.org/tourofwebauthn/tourofwebauthn.pdf) (and the broader 2025 IACR analysis) note that the model is "one credential per RP," so loss is local, not catastrophic.

EUDI Wallet recovery is part of the ARF. The Member State issues the wallet; recovery is implemented by re-issuance after identity proofing. Because wallets are mobile and rely on WSCDs, the practical recovery story will depend on member-state implementation by the end-2026 deadline.

Aadhaar recovery is biometric-based: the user can re-authenticate at any of the thousands of Aadhaar centres using their enrolled biometrics plus demographic data. The [Aadhaar Authentication API 1.6](https://uidai.gov.in/images/resource/aadhaar_authentication_api_2_5.pdf) treats every authentication as a yes/no against the CIDR; a lost VID is regenerated.

Estonia's recovery is similarly identity-based: a new ID-card or Mobile-ID is issued by the Police and Border Guard Board after in-person verification ([RIA eID page](https://www.ria.ee/en/state-information-system/electronic-identity-eid-and-trust-services/electronic-identity-eid)). The 2017 ID-card crypto vulnerability required mass remote re-keying and demonstrates the operational reality.

### 3.5 Suitability by Use Case

#### 3.5.1 Banking

- **Strongest fit: FIDO2/WebAuthn** with a VC layer for KYC. WebAuthn's phishing resistance (origin bound in CollectedClientData) and RP-scoped keys match PSD2 SCA in the EU. Major banks have deployed FIDO2 for employee and consumer authentication.
- **EUDI Wallet** is positioned for regulated KYC under [eIDAS 2.0](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1183/oj); PID + bank-issued EAA replaces paper KYC, with selective disclosure reducing over-sharing.
- **Aadhaar** is the dominant banking KYC in India. The [Press Information Bureau October 2024 release](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2067940&lang=2&reg=3) reports "788 Million Aadhaar have been uniquely linked with the bank accounts on NPCI mapper" as of end-July 2023. After the 2018 Supreme Court ruling, Aadhaar cannot be mandatory for opening bank accounts, but it is used voluntarily.
- **Estonia e-Residency** is the dominant case: e-residents open and operate Estonian companies entirely remotely, with digital signatures on every document. In 2024, e-residents founded ~1 in 5 new Estonian companies ([Baltic Times 2024](https://www.baltictimes.com/new_milestone_for-e-residency-with_record_number_of_companies_founded_in_2024/)).
- **W3C DIDs/VCs** are nascent in banking. Sovrin, IDunion, and similar networks are piloting but no major bank has a production deployment at scale.

#### 3.5.2 Healthcare

- **Strongest fit: W3C VCs + EUDI Wallet.** The [HL7 SMART Health Cards IG](https://hl7.org/fhir/uv/smart-health-cards-and-links/STU1/cards-credential-modeling.html) "describes how clinical information, modeled in FHIR, can be presented in a form based on W3C Verifiable Credentials (VC)," and SMART Health Cards were deployed at scale for COVID-19 vaccination credentials. The W3C [VC Use Cases](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-use-cases/) catalog uses including "Online pharmacy" (verifying physician credential + patient insurance) and "Traveling illness" (cross-border health presentation).
- **EUDI Wallet** will support medical prescriptions, EHDS (European Health Data Space) attestations, and cross-border health data exchange; the ARF treats this as a flagship scenario.
- **Aadhaar** is used for linking health records via the ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) number, leveraging the 1.418 billion Aadhaar base. However, Aadhaar's centralisation means every health-record linkage is potentially correlatable, which is a significant concern in sensitive domains like HIV status, mental health, or reproductive care.
- **FIDO2/WebAuthn** is the right tool for clinician authentication to an EHR but not for portable health credentials.
- **Estonia's e-Health system** uses X-Road to give clinicians queryable access to a central e-Health record; e-Residency is not itself a healthcare credential.

#### 3.5.3 Humanitarian Aid for Stateless Populations

This is the most demanding use case because:
1. The subject often has no state-issued foundational ID.
2. Privacy is existential — biometric data in hostile regimes can be lethal.
3. Recovery infrastructure may not exist.
4. The population is mobile.

- **W3C DIDs/VCs** have the strongest conceptual fit. UNHCR has been [accepting proposals on digital identity since November 2018](https://www.unhcr.org/blogs/unhcr-accepting-proposals-digital-identity/), explicitly referencing "self-managed Digital Wallet for refugees." UNHCR PRIMES "holds identity records of more than 8 million refugees globally" but "None of these data elements is currently accessible, neither in parts nor in total to refugees or asylum seekers" — exactly the asymmetry VCs invert. The [Sovrin Foundation report "Distributed ledger identification systems in the humanitarian sector"](https://sovrin.org/wp-content/uploads/14A-Report.pdf) analyses the IFRC-KRCS Blockchain Open Loop Cash Transfer Pilot and WFP Building Blocks, concluding that DLT-based identification can shift control to beneficiaries if designed carefully.
- **WFP Building Blocks** used a permissioned blockchain for Syrian refugee cash transfers in Jordan; the [Blockchange analysis](https://blockchan.ge/blockchange-resource-provision.pdf) describes it as addressing "single point of failure" of voucher/credit card systems.
- **UNHCR-Stellar Aid Assist** ([Stellar case study](https://stellar.org/case-studies/unhcr)) delivered USDC stablecoin aid to IDPs in Ukraine, with UNHCR confirming eligibility and disbursing through the Vibrant digital wallet.
- **DIGID (Red Cross digital wallet)** is being piloted in Kenya and Uganda for refugees and IDPs ([Red Social Innovation](https://red-social-innovation.com/en/solution/digid-digital-wallet-refugees/)).
- **Aadhaar** cannot serve undocumented populations because enrolment requires identity proofing; however, the ID4Africa 2026 session ([UNHCR press release](https://www.unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/unhcr-calls-universal-inclusion-refugees-stateless-persons-and-people-risk)) reports progress in Chad, Côte d'Ivoire, Kenya, Mali, Namibia, and Uganda on "statelessness-sensitive" designs that *extend* national IDs to refugees and stateless persons habitually resident in the country.
- **Estonia e-Residency** is not designed for stateless populations — it requires a background check against a partner state's documents.
- **FIDO2/WebAuthn** is insufficient as a primary identity layer for stateless persons; it requires a pre-existing relying-party account.

Crucially, the [UNSW Kaldor Centre commentary on the Rohingya](https://www.unsw.edu.au/kaldor-centre/our-resources/legal-and-policy-resources/commentaries/diversity-and-inclusion-blockchain-technology-and-digital-identity-stateless-rohingya) emphasises that "the international community and non-governmental organizations (NGOs), nor internal local authorities, have not been able to promote sustainable peace and security." Technology choices are constrained by political realities — a blockchain ID for the Rohingya in Myanmar would not protect them from the state that denies their citizenship.

Quick comparative proportions:
- **Aadhaar / India population (1.4 B) ≈ 17.6% of world population** (8.05 B). UIDAI's claim of "nearly every sixth person in the world holding this unique identification" ([PIB Oct 2024](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2067940&lang=2&reg=3)) is consistent with the 1.418 B / 8 B figure (≈17.7%).
- **815 M breach records / 1.418 B enrolled ≈ 57.5%** of all Aadhaar numbers potentially exposed in the single largest reported incident.

## 5. Synthesis and Conclusions

1. **No single system is optimal for all use cases.** The taxonomy collapses to: state-foundational IDs (Aadhaar, Estonia) for populations with a state; decentralised IDs (DIDs/VCs) for populations *without* a state or for cross-organisational attribute exchange; strong authentication (FIDO2/WebAuthn) as a complementary *authentication* layer rather than an identity *issuance* layer; regulated identity wallets (EUDI) as a hybrid that hardens the centralised model with selective disclosure and ZKP.

2. **FIDO2/WebAuthn is the most operationally mature technical standard for authentication.** It has been formally analysed in [IACR ePrint 2025/459](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/459.pdf), has near-universal browser and platform support, and provides phishing resistance via origin binding. It should be a default component of any system, not a competing alternative.

3. **W3C DIDs/VCs have the strongest theoretical privacy posture but the weakest real-world interoperability and recovery story.** Method fragmentation is severe, recovery is non-standard (still in [W3C-CCG draft](https://github.com/w3c-ccg/did-recovery)), and issuer ecosystems are nascent. They are the right choice for humanitarian and stateless use cases because they require no state registration.

4. **EUDI Wallet is a major attempt to graft W3C-style selective disclosure onto a state-issued model.** Whether the [ARF v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0) achieves its privacy goals depends on implementation by 27+ Member States by end of 2026, on ZKP scheme selection (BBS+ is under IRTF standardisation per [TS4](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-standards-and-technical-specifications/blob/main/docs/technical-specifications/ts4-zkp.md)), and on the legal regime around the 2024 Implementing Regulations.

5. **Aadhaar demonstrates the centralisation trade-off at scale.** With 1.418 B numbers and 95% penetration, it is unmatched in coverage but the 815 M-record breach demonstrates the cost of centralisation. The 2018 Supreme Court ruling attempted to bound surveillance risk by striking private use and limiting retention, but the underlying architecture is fixed.

6. **Estonia demonstrates that a state-issued PKI can be operationally robust and privacy-respecting** *if* the surrounding legal and technical audit (X-Road, KSI, data embassies) is built with the same care as the credential itself. The e-Residency program shows the model can be exported digitally (144,000+ users globally) but the revenue claims (€66.8M for 2024) are partially contested ([ERR News 2024](https://news.err.ee/1609279218/estonian-e-residency-success-metrics-impossible-to-verify)).

7. **For humanitarian and stateless populations, the practical frontier is identity provision without a state.** The combination of W3C VCs (for portable, self-issued claims by NGOs and UNHCR) plus a FIDO2-based wallet (for local device authentication) plus optional anchoring to a state-foundational ID when available (per the [UNHCR ID4Africa 2026 work](https://www.unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/unhcr-calls-universal-inclusion-refugees-stateless-persons-and-people-risk)) is the most defensible architecture. The Sovrin/WFP/UNHCR-Stellar pilots in Syria, Jordan, and Ukraine provide empirical evidence that such systems can deliver aid at scale, though governance — not cryptography — remains the harder problem.

**Source uncertainty / caveats.** The 815 M Aadhaar breach figure is from a security-firm report and a [press account](https://coercioncode.com/2024/04/12/the-worlds-largest-biometric-digital-id-system-indias-aadhaar-is-hacked-nearly-10-of-the-world-population/); UIDAI has not publicly confirmed the scale. EUDI Wallet interoperability is projected, not yet observed. The DID recovery specifications cited ([W3C-CCG](https://github.com/w3c-ccg/did-recovery), [Sirraya Labs DID-KR](https://github.com/sirraya-labs/did-kr)) are CG drafts, not W3C Recommendations. The Estonia revenue claims rest on EISA's methodology, which an [ERR News investigation](https://news.err.ee/1609279218/estonian-e-residency-success-metrics-impossible-to-verify) found unverifiable.
